title: Plots and Live Graphs
summary: A number that changes every frame is hard to read; a graph of its last few seconds is easy. This lesson covers ImGui's built-in `PlotLines` and `PlotHistogram`, the ring buffer that feeds them, scaling and statistics, drawing your own graph with the draw list, and when to reach for the ImPlot library.
ideas:
- Add a frame-time graph with a fixed 0 to 33 ms scale and an overlay of the average and maximum.
- Draw a custom graph with two lines (CPU and GPU time) and the 16.6 ms budget line.

cards.q: How does a ring buffer feed a scrolling graph?
cards.a:
New samples overwrite the oldest; the offset says where the oldest sample is

Nothing moves in the fixed array: the write position goes round it, and `values_offset` tells PlotLines to start drawing at the oldest sample.

cards.q: Name two ways to smooth a noisy value.
cards.a:
A moving average over the last N samples, and exponential smoothing: `smoothed += (value - smoothed) * k`

The moving average uses the samples already in the ring buffer; exponential smoothing needs no buffer at all.

cards.q: How do you map a value to a y position in a custom graph?
cards.a:
`y = top + height * (1 - (value - min) / (max - min))`

Screen y grows downwards, so the fraction is flipped with `1 -`: larger values get smaller y and appear higher.

cards.q: What is the `values_offset` argument of PlotLines for?
cards.a:
It says where the oldest sample of a ring buffer is, so the graph scrolls without moving data

Pass the ring buffer's write position once it is full.

cards.q: A ring buffer of 120 samples is full and its next write position is 37. Where is the oldest sample?
cards.a:
At index 37

The next write overwrites the oldest sample, so the oldest is where the next write will go. Index 36 is the newest.

cards.q: When should you use ImPlot instead of PlotLines?
cards.a:
When you need axes, zooming, legends or several series

PlotLines is a quick single-series graph; ImPlot is a companion library with its own context for full charts.
